headline: A Senate bill that would have created a federal legal right to contraception was blocked on June 5, 2024.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this bill would have set a right to contraception in federal law. No official summary is available, so the exact rules, protections, and enforcement details are not described here. On June 5, 2024, the Senate did not get enough votes to end debate and move forward, so the bill did not pass.

who_it_affects.group: People who use or want to use birth control
who_it_affects.how: They would have gained a right to contraception written into federal law.

who_it_affects.group: Health care providers who offer birth control
who_it_affects.how: They would likely have been affected by a federal right to contraception, though the details are not described in the available material.
